hartlib.lead: Hartlib is one research chat over everything you subscribe to, for people who read professional briefings.
points: Answers plain-language questions with each claim linked to its page
Reads dense briefings, letters and official records for you
Lets publishers publish issues and invite client companies

silo.lead: Silo gives your AI agents their own isolated computers to do real work, with a desktop and computer use.
points: Runs each agent in its own sandbox so they can build, install tools and execute code without touching your host
Watch agents work live on a real desktop, or let them drive browsers and graphical apps via computer use
Save instant checkpoints to roll an agent back when things break, or fork machines to work in parallel

lcu.lead: LCU lets AI agents outside the Codex app use Codex's computer control to work your desktop apps.
points: Read windows, click, type and take screenshots in desktop apps
Approve or deny each app the first time an agent tries to use it
Read and control Chrome tabs through the official extension

fjord.lead: Fjord sits between your Claude Code sessions and GitHub, and brings you only what you need to know or decide.
points: Answer every Claude Code session's questions and plans from one page
Sort your GitHub inbox and CI by rules you write as sentences
Hand a failing check to the Claude Code session that can fix it

sic.lead: Sic checks the facts in French political debates against official sources, live or on replay.
points: Turns debate audio into text and names who is speaking
Picks out checkable claims and skips opinions and promises
Gives no verdict without a cited source and a precise link

lastdrop.lead: lastdrop lets Claude Code call any model as its own subagent and spreads the work across your accounts.
points: Switches to the next model when one runs out of quota or can't start
Checks every command an agent runs instead of asking you to approve it
Shows usage left on each account and when it resets
